```{r}
#| label: setup
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(CanadaForestAllometry)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
```

# Introduction

The package currently includes
`r length(unique(si_model_registry()$engine))` site-index model functions,
covering a wide range of tree species, provinces and territories, and stand
types, including natural stands and plantations. They range from
Lundgren and Dolid's **1970** models [@LundgrenDolid1970] to
Huang et al.'s **2026** models [@HuangEtAl2026].

Most follow the same logic: estimate site index from age and height, or
predict height from age and site index. However, the definitions differ.
Some use **total age**, others **breast-height age** (years since reaching
1.3 m). The package also groups years since planting under total age for
models that use it, including Auger-Ward and Prégent. The reference
age is most commonly **50 years**, but some models use 25 years or another
age. Height may mean top height measured from the ground, or height above
breast height. These differences matter when choosing a model and
interpreting its results.

Each model is implemented following its publication, without modifying
the published equations or coefficients.

# Using `si()` {#si-dispatcher}

To make these models easier to use, `si()` selects a suitable model for
each observation from the available age-height models. In addition to
`age`, `height` or `si`, and `species`, it needs:

- `jurisdiction`: the province or territory, such as `"QC"` or `"BC"`;
- `input_age_basis`: how age was measured, usually `"total_age"` or
  `"breast_height_age"`;
- `stand_origin`: `"natural"` or `"plantation"` for automatic selection.

Some models also need regional information, such as `bec_zone` in British
Columbia or `natural_subregion` in Alberta. Ages are in years; heights and
site indices are in metres. Species use NFI codes, such as `"PICE.GLA"`
for white spruce.

For Auger-Ward and Prégent models, use `input_age_basis = "total_age"` and
supply years since planting. The function uses these ages as supplied,
without adding or subtracting nursery years.

## Estimate site index from measured height

For example, estimate site index for two white spruce observations from
plantations in Quebec, with age measured since planting:

```{r}
#| label: si-estimation-example
si_estimates <- si(
  age = c(20, 30),
  height = c(10, 15),
  species = "PICE.GLA",
  jurisdiction = "QC",
  input_age_basis = "total_age",
  stand_origin = "plantation"
)

si_estimates |>
  dplyr::select(si, model_id, reference_age, status)
```

The result includes the estimated `si`, the selected `model_id`, its
`reference_age` and a `status` indicating whether the prediction succeeded.
Here, the selected model is `pregent2010`, which uses a reference age of
**25 years since planting**. You can supply several observations at once;
shared values such as species and jurisdiction only need to be supplied once.

## Predict height from site index

When supplying site index, the simplest option is to give the `model_id`
of the model used to estimate it. A value such as `si = 18` could refer to
height at age 25 or 50, with age measured since planting or at breast height.
The model ID identifies these definitions and keeps height predictions
consistent with the model used to estimate site index.

For example, predict height for a white spruce plantation with a Pregent
site index of 18 m at 25 years since planting:

```{r}
#| label: si-height-example
si(
  age = c(20, 30, 40),
  si = 18,
  species = "PICE.GLA",
  jurisdiction = "QC",
  input_age_basis = "total_age",
  stand_origin = "plantation",
  model_id = "pregent2010"
) |>
  dplyr::select(height, model_id, reference_age, status)
```

Alternatively, you can omit `model_id` if you explicitly supply the SI
reference age (`reference_age`), its age type (`reference_age_basis`),
whether SI height is measured from the ground or above breast height
(`si_datum`), and whether the value is site index or height index
(`productivity_quantity`). In this case, `si()` warns because models with
the same definitions can still predict different heights at other ages.

Keep the same model when predicting heights at different ages: a site-index
value from one model should not simply be used in another. `si()` does not
convert between age types or height definitions. If no suitable model is
available, it returns a missing prediction with a warning; the `reason`
column explains why.

Growth-intercept models, ecological-site curves and climate-dependent models
are used through their individual functions rather than `si()`.

# Finding models and their inputs

`find_si_models()` helps you explore models for your species and jurisdiction
and see which additional inputs they need. In this example,
`"infer_si_from_height"` means estimating site index from measured height:

```{r}
#| label: si-discovery-example
find_si_models(
  jurisdiction = "QC",
  species = "PICE.GLA",
  operation = "infer_si_from_height",
  available = c("age", "height"),
  input_age_basis = "total_age",
  stand_origin = "plantation"
) |>
  dplyr::select(model_id, discovery_status, missing_predictors)
```

The results also include models that do not match your inputs, so this is a
browsing tool rather than a list of recommended models.

Use `get_si_model_info()` to look up an individual model:

```{r}
#| label: si-info-example
info <- get_si_model_info("pregent2010")
info$description
info$species
info$native_defaults$base_age
```

Here, `base_age` is the reference age used by the model. For a full list of
models and their age types, use `si_model_registry()`:

```{r}
#| label: si-registry-example
si_model_registry() |>
  dplyr::select(model_id, engine, age_basis)
```

# Site index models included in the package

The sections below briefly describe each function and illustrate its
height-age curves where available. Numbers beside the curves are site-index
values. Follow the function-reference links for arguments and usage details.

```{r}
#| label: si-model-sections
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: asis

si_age_axis_label <- function(model_row) {
  if (model_row$model_id[[1]] %in% c("augerward2021", "pregent2010", "pregent2016")) {
    return("Total age (years since planting)")
  }
  evidence <- model_row$metadata_evidence[[1]]
  disputed_input <- evidence$status == "unresolved" & evidence$subject %in% c(
    "input_age_basis", "input_and_reference_age", "input_and_reference_age_basis",
    "species_age_basis_and_recommendation"
  )
  if (any(disputed_input)) {
    return("Age (years)")
  }
  switch(
    model_row$age_basis[[1]],
    total_age = "Total age (years)",
    breast_height_age = "Breast-height age (years)",
    corrected_age_above_1m = "Corrected age above 1 m (years)",
    species_dependent = "Age (years; type varies by species)",
    unresolved = "Age (years)",
    stop("Unknown SI input age basis.")
  )
}

plot_si_curves <- function(
  model_row,
  si_values = c(5, 10, 15, 20, 25),
  age_min = 1,
  age_max = 150,
  age_by = 1,
  subregion = "All",
  climate = NULL,
  facet_ncol = 4
) {
  model_name <- model_row$engine[[1]]
  model_fun <- get(model_name, mode = "function")
  supports_predict_height <- model_row$supports_predict_height[[1]]
  species_vec <- model_row$species[[1]]
  age_domain_max <- model_row$age_domain_max[[1]]
  plot_si_values <- model_row$plot_si_values[[1]]
  x_axis_label <- si_age_axis_label(model_row)
  definitions <- model_row$scientific_definitions[[1]]
  native <- definitions[definitions$condition %in% c("native", "total_height=TRUE"), ]
  y_axis_label <- if (any(native$height_datum == "unresolved")) {
    "Height (m)"
  } else if (any(native$height_datum == "above_breast_height")) {
    "Height above breast height (m)"
  } else if (any(native$productivity_quantity %in% c("height_index", "inherent_height_index"))) {
    "Dominant/codominant tree height (m)"
  } else {
    "Height (m)"
  }

  if (!isTRUE(supports_predict_height) || isTRUE(model_row$requires_gi[[1]])) {
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
      ggplot2::annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, label = "Height curve not available for this model") +
      ggplot2::xlim(0, 1) +
      ggplot2::ylim(0, 1) +
      ggplot2::theme_void() +
      ggplot2::ggtitle(paste0(model_name, "()"))
    return(list(plot = p, n_rows = 1L, n_species = 0L))
  }

  call_fixed <- model_row$fixed_args[[1]]

  if (!is.na(age_domain_max)) {
    age_max <- min(age_max, age_domain_max)
  }
  if (!is.null(plot_si_values)) {
    si_values <- plot_si_values
  }

  ages <- seq(age_min, age_max, by = age_by)
  grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(
    species = species_vec,
    si = si_values,
    age = ages
  )
  if (!is.null(climate)) {
    grid <- dplyr::left_join(grid, climate, by = dplyr::join_by(species))
    climate_args <- c("MAP", "MWMT", "MAP_normal", "MWMT_normal")
    if (anyNA(grid[climate_args])) {
      stop("Climate scenario must supply all four inputs for every plotted species.")
    }
  } else {
    climate_args <- character()
  }

  prediction_errors <- character()
  pred_one <- function(i) {
    args <- c(
      list(age = grid$age[[i]], si = grid$si[[i]]),
      if ("species" %in% names(formals(model_fun))) list(species = grid$species[[i]]) else list(),
      if ("natural_subregion" %in% names(formals(model_fun))) list(natural_subregion = subregion) else list(),
      call_fixed,
      as.list(grid[i, climate_args, drop = FALSE])
    )
    out <- tryCatch(
      do.call(model_fun, args),
      error = function(e) {
        prediction_errors <<- unique(c(prediction_errors, conditionMessage(e)))
        NULL
      }
    )
    if (is.null(out) || !"height" %in% names(out)) return(NA_real_)
    as.numeric(out$height[[1]])
  }

  grid$height <- vapply(
    seq_len(nrow(grid)),
    pred_one,
    numeric(1)
  )

  plot_data <- grid |>
    dplyr::filter(is.finite(.data$height)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(si = factor(.data$si, levels = sort(unique(si_values))))

  if (nrow(plot_data) == 0L) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "No height predictions for %s: %s",
      model_row$model_id[[1]], paste(prediction_errors, collapse = "; ")
    ))
  }
  if (length(prediction_errors)) {
    cat(
      "**Some curve points were omitted after prediction errors:** ",
      paste(prediction_errors, collapse = "; "), "\n\n", sep = ""
    )
  }
  label_data <- plot_data |>
    dplyr::group_by(.data$species, .data$si) |>
    dplyr::filter(.data$age == max(.data$age, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
    dplyr::slice_tail(n = 1) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()

  n_species <- length(species_vec)
  n_rows <- max(1L, ceiling(n_species / facet_ncol))
  n_panels <- n_rows * facet_ncol

  species_plots <- lapply(species_vec, function(sp) {
    df_sp <- plot_data |>
      dplyr::filter(.data$species == sp)
    lab_sp <- label_data |>
      dplyr::filter(.data$species == sp)

    ggplot2::ggplot(
      df_sp,
      ggplot2::aes(x = .data$age, y = .data$height, group = .data$si)
    ) +
      ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.6, color = "black") +
      ggplot2::geom_text(
        data = lab_sp,
        ggplot2::aes(label = .data$si),
        size = 2.2,
        hjust = -0.15,
        color = "black"
      ) +
      ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
        limits = c(0, age_max),
        breaks = seq(0, age_max, by = 25),
        expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))
      ) +
      ggplot2::labs(
        title = sp,
        x = x_axis_label,
        y = y_axis_label
      ) +
      ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
  })

  if (n_panels > n_species) {
    species_plots <- c(
      species_plots,
      replicate(n_panels - n_species, patchwork::plot_spacer(), simplify = FALSE)
    )
  }

  p <- patchwork::wrap_plots(species_plots, ncol = facet_ncol)

  list(plot = p, n_rows = n_rows, n_species = n_species)
}

plot_lafleche_examples <- function(model_row, facet_ncol = 4) {
  curve_set <- model_row$fixed_args[[1]]$curve_set

  example_keys <- tibble::tribble(
    ~species,     ~ecological_region, ~ecological_subregion, ~ecological_type, ~label,
    "ABIE.BAL",   "3c",               NA_character_,         "MJ12",           "ABIE.BAL",
    "PICE.GLA",   "2a",               NA_character_,         "MJ11",           "PICE.GLA",
    "THUJ.OCC",   "4f",               NA_character_,         "RS12",           "THUJ.OCC",
    "ABIE.BAL",   "5e",               "5eT",                 "MS22",           "ABIE.BAL (5eT)"
  )

  ages <- seq(1, 150, by = 1)
  grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(example_id = seq_len(nrow(example_keys)), age = ages) |>
    dplyr::left_join(
      dplyr::mutate(example_keys, example_id = seq_len(dplyr::n())),
      by = "example_id"
    )

  pred <- si_lafleche2013(
    age = grid$age,
    species = grid$species,
    ecological_region = grid$ecological_region,
    ecological_type = grid$ecological_type,
    ecological_subregion = grid$ecological_subregion,
    curve_set = curve_set
  )

  plot_data <- dplyr::bind_cols(grid, pred)
  label_data <- plot_data |>
    dplyr::group_by(.data$label) |>
    dplyr::slice_max(.data$age, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()

  species_plots <- lapply(example_keys$label, function(sp) {
    df_sp <- plot_data |>
      dplyr::filter(.data$label == sp)
    lab_sp <- label_data |>
      dplyr::filter(.data$label == sp)

    ggplot2::ggplot(
      df_sp,
      ggplot2::aes(x = .data$age, y = .data$height)
    ) +
      ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.6, color = "black") +
      ggplot2::geom_text(
        data = lab_sp,
        ggplot2::aes(label = sprintf("IQS %.2f", .data$si)),
        size = 2.2,
        hjust = -0.15,
        color = "black"
      ) +
      ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
        limits = c(0, 150),
        breaks = seq(0, 150, by = 25),
        expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))
      ) +
      ggplot2::labs(
        title = sp,
        x = si_age_axis_label(model_row),
        y = "Height (m)"
      ) +
      ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
  })

  p <- patchwork::wrap_plots(species_plots, ncol = facet_ncol)

  list(plot = p, n_rows = 1L, n_species = nrow(example_keys))
}

reg <- CanadaForestAllometry:::si_model_registry_species() |>
  dplyr::arrange(.data$engine, .data$model_id)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(reg))) {
  x <- reg[i, , drop = FALSE]
  first_variant <- i == 1L || x$engine[[1]] != reg$engine[[i - 1L]]
  multiple_variants <- sum(reg$engine == x$engine[[1]]) > 1L
  ref_fun_link <- paste0("[`", x$engine, "()`](../reference/", x$engine, ".html)")
  if (first_variant) {
    cat("## `", x$engine[[1]], "()`\n\n", sep = "")
    cat("- Function reference: ", ref_fun_link, "\n\n", sep = "")
  }
  if (multiple_variants) {
    variant_label <- switch(
      x$model_id[[1]],
      huang2026 = "Non-climate",
      huang2026_climate = "Climate-sensitive",
      paste0("`", x$model_id[[1]], "`")
    )
    cat("### ", variant_label, "\n\n", sep = "")
  }

  coverage <- if (any(x$province_scope[[1]] == "ALL")) {
    "Canada (all provinces/territories)"
  } else {
    paste(x$province_scope[[1]], collapse = ", ")
  }

  species_cov <- if (length(x$species[[1]]) == 0L) {
    "unknown"
  } else {
    paste(x$species[[1]], collapse = ", ")
  }

  age_basis_text <- si_age_axis_label(x)

  description_text <- switch(
    x$engine[[1]],
    si_alemdag1991 = "Canada-wide model for white spruce in natural stands",
    si_augerward2021 = "Jack pine and black spruce plantations in Quebec",
    si_batho2014 = "Lodgepole pine in British Columbia",
    si_brisco2002 = "Western larch in British Columbia",
    si_buckman2006 = "Red pine site-index model",
    si_carmean1989 = "Site-index models for eastern tree species",
    si_carmean1996 = "Site-index models for northwestern Ontario",
    si_carmean2001 = "Jack pine in northern Ontario",
    si_carmean2006 = "Black spruce and trembling aspen in northwestern Ontario",
    si_carmeanhahn1981 = "Balsam fir and white spruce site-index models",
    si_chenklinka2000 = "Subalpine fir, Engelmann spruce and lodgepole pine in British Columbia",
    si_cieszewski1993 = "Site-index models for eleven Saskatchewan species",
    si_cieszewskibella1991 = "Site-index models for four Alberta species",
    si_goelz1992 = "Jack pine in north-central Ontario",
    si_goudie1984 = "Lodgepole pine and white spruce in British Columbia",
    si_huang1994 = "Site-index models for Alberta tree species",
    si_huang2009 = "Top-height and site-index models for four Alberta species",
    si_huang2026 = "Height-age models for eight Alberta species, with and without climate inputs",
    si_hugarcia2009 = "Interior spruce in British Columbia",
    si_kerbowling1991 = "Softwood site-index models for New Brunswick",
    si_lafleche2013 = "Height curves based on species and ecological classification in Quebec",
    si_lundgrendolid1970 = "Two alternative curve forms for several Lake States tree species",
    si_nigh1997 = "Sitka spruce in coastal British Columbia",
    si_nigh1998 = "Western hemlock in interior British Columbia",
    si_nigh1998_gi = "Estimates site index from annual height growth for western hemlock",
    si_nigh2000 = "Western redcedar in interior British Columbia",
    si_nigh2000_gi = "Estimates site index from annual height growth for western redcedar",
    si_nigh2002 = "Trembling aspen in British Columbia",
    si_nigh2004 = "Young lodgepole pine and interior spruce in British Columbia",
    si_nigh2009 = "Paper birch in British Columbia",
    si_nigh2017 = "Lodgepole pine in British Columbia",
    si_nighcourtin1998 = "Red alder, with site index expressed at age 25 or 50",
    si_parresolvissage1998 = "Eastern white pine site-index model",
    si_payandeh1974 = "Site-index models for several North American tree species",
    si_pregent2010 = "White spruce plantations in Quebec",
    si_pregent2016 = "Norway spruce plantations in Quebec",
    si_scottvoorhis1986 = "Site-index models accepting total or breast-height age",
    si_sharma2015 = "Jack pine and black spruce plantations",
    si_sharma2021 = "Jack pine and black spruce in mixed stands",
    si_sharma2022 = "Black spruce and trembling aspen in mixed stands",
    si_sharmaparton2018a = "White spruce plantations",
    si_sharmaparton2018b = "Red pine plantations",
    si_sharmaparton2019 = "White pine plantations",
    si_sharmareid2018 = "Jack pine and black spruce in natural stands",
    si_thrower1994 = "Site-index models for interior British Columbia species",
    x$description[[1]]
  )

  cat("- Model ID: `", x$model_id[[1]], "`\n", sep = "")
  cat("- Description: ", description_text, "\n", sep = "")
  cat("- Reference: ", x$reference[[1]], "\n", sep = "")
  cat("- Age type: ", age_basis_text, "\n", sep = "")
  cat("- Coverage: ", coverage, "\n", sep = "")
  cat("- Species coverage: ", species_cov, "\n", sep = "")
  cat("\n", sep = "")

  if (any(x$fixed_arg_roles[[1]] == "plot_only")) {
    cat(
      "The figure uses a reference age of 50 years (`base_age = 50`); ",
      "the function's default is 25 years since planting.\n\n", sep = ""
    )
  }

  if (!isTRUE(x$supports_predict_height[[1]]) || isTRUE(x$requires_gi[[1]])) {
    cat("_No height curve graphic is available for this variant._\n\n")
    cat("\n\n")
    next
  }

  scenarios <- list(default = NULL)
  if (identical(x$model_id[[1]], "huang2026")) {
    cat(
      "This version predicts height without climate inputs, using a height ",
      "index at 50 years total age.\n\n",
      sep = ""
    )
  }
  if (identical(x$model_id[[1]], "huang2026_climate")) {
    cat(
      "This version also requires precipitation and warmest-month temperature, ",
      "plus their long-term averages; see the function reference for inputs. ",
      "The figures compare two illustrative, fixed climate settings: ",
      "reference conditions, and 10% less precipitation with a 1 degree C ",
      "warmer warmest month. Labels show the model's climate-adjusted height ",
      "index, not necessarily height at age 50. These are illustrations, ",
      "not forecasts of growth under changing climate.\n\n",
      sep = ""
    )
    normals <- tibble::tribble(
      ~species, ~MAP_normal, ~MWMT_normal,
      "POPU.TRE", 500, 15.5,
      "PICE.GLA", 500, 15,
      "PINU.CON", 625, 14,
      "PICE.MAR", 550, 15,
      "POPU.BAL", 550, 15,
      "ABIE.BAL", 625, 14,
      "PSEU.MEN", 625, 14.5,
      "PINU.BAN", 450, 16.5
    )
    scenarios <- list(
      at_normals = dplyr::mutate(normals, MAP = MAP_normal, MWMT = MWMT_normal),
      warmer_drier = dplyr::mutate(
        normals, MAP = 0.9 * MAP_normal, MWMT = MWMT_normal + 1
      )
    )
  }

  for (scenario in names(scenarios)) {
    if (length(scenarios) > 1L) {
      scenario_label <- switch(
        scenario,
        at_normals = "Climate averages equal the reference normals",
        warmer_drier = "Warmer/drier: MAP 10% lower, MWMT 1 degree C higher"
      )
      cat("#### ", scenario_label, "\n\n", sep = "")
    }
    if (identical(x$engine[[1]], "si_lafleche2013")) {
      curve_set <- x$fixed_args[[1]]$curve_set
      cat(
        "This model predicts height from species and ecological classification. ",
        "The figure shows examples from the ", curve_set, " curve set.\n\n",
        sep = ""
      )

      plot_out <- plot_lafleche_examples(model_row = x, facet_ncol = 4)
    } else {
      plot_out <- plot_si_curves(
        model_row = x,
        si_values = c(5, 10, 15, 20, 25),
        age_min = 1,
        age_max = 150,
        age_by = 1,
        subregion = "All",
        climate = scenarios[[scenario]],
        facet_ncol = 4
      )
    }

    p <- plot_out$plot +
      patchwork::plot_annotation(
        title = x$model_id[[1]],
        subtitle = if (length(scenarios) > 1L) scenario_label else NULL
      )

    fig_dir <- knitr::opts_chunk$get("fig.path")
    dir.create(fig_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    file_stub <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_-]", "-", paste(x$model_id[[1]], scenario, sep = "-"))
    fig_file <- file.path(fig_dir, paste0("si-curves-", file_stub, ".png"))
    fig_file_out <- gsub("\\\\", "/", fig_file)

    row_height <- 2.3
    fig_h <- max(2.8, row_height * plot_out$n_rows)

    ggplot2::ggsave(
      filename = fig_file,
      plot = p,
      width = 10,
      height = fig_h,
      dpi = 140,
      bg = "white"
    )

    cat("![](", fig_file_out, ")\n\n", sep = "")
    cat("\n\n")
  }
}
```

# References
